concerns.concern: The authors do not consider that the effect may be ordinary quench-disordered metastable vortex matter in a single superconducting phase, as in NbSe2 and other peak-effect systems. They cite none of that literature and do not perform standard tests such as field-cooled versus zero-field-cooled Jc or field-history protocols, so the novelty claim is unsupported.
concerns.quote: The leading alternative explanation, quench-disordered metastable vortex matter in a single superconducting phase, is not considered, and the novelty claim depends on excluding it.

concerns.concern: The data contain a peak-effect signature: a hump in V(B) at fixed J near 7–12 T, where the memory sits. The authors should check whether the memory window coincides with a Jc(B) peak or trough on the same sample.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4b shows a non-monotonic V(B) at fixed J, with a hump near 7–12 T where the memory sits. This is the textbook transport signature of a peak effect.

concerns.concern: The authors should state explicitly which observation, if any, requires two order parameters rather than generic vortex metastability.
concerns.quote: State explicitly which observation, if any, requires two order parameters.

concerns.concern: The memory field range does not match SC1/SC2 coexistence. In sample S2 the memory peaks near 10 T and has vanished by about 17 T, well inside SC1, whereas coexistence is placed at 15–20 T.
concerns.quote: Explain why an effect attributed to coexistence peaks about 10 T below the phase boundary.

concerns.concern: The phase diagrams are taken from a reference on ultraclean crystals rather than measured on the samples studied, one of which has much lower RRR. The SC1/SC2 boundary and Hc2(θ) should be mapped on the same samples.
concerns.quote: The phase diagrams in Figs. 1a and 4a come from ref. 33, which concerns ultraclean crystals. They are not measured on S1 or S2.

concerns.concern: The full field dependence of the memory is not shown for sample S1, so it is unclear whether its window resembles S2's. The windows differ substantially even though the text calls the sample difference slight.
concerns.quote: Show the full B-dependence of ΔJ for S1.

concerns.concern: The angular argument is made at 15 T, where SC2 is not adjacent even at zero tilt. The coincidence of the roughly 20° cutoff with the angular extent of SC2 therefore does not link the two.
concerns.quote: The argument is made at 15 T, where SC2 is not adjacent even at θ = 0.

concerns.concern: Joule and contact heating during pumps is not excluded. No sample dimensions, contact resistances or dissipated power are given, and even about 1 Ω at 40 mA would far exceed the fridge cooling power.
concerns.quote: At 40 mA, even about 1 Ω of contact resistance gives about 1.6 mW. That is orders of magnitude above typical mixing-chamber cooling power at 50 mK.

concerns.concern: The three arguments against heating fail. The turn-off-rate dependence is exactly what a thermal quench predicts, field and angle selectivity only shows a metastable window exists, and the loss at higher T concerns stability rather than writing. A current-free heater-pulse control and equal-energy comparisons are needed.
concerns.quote: The turn-off-rate dependence is exactly what a *thermal* quench predicts.

concerns.concern: Thermometer location and time resolution are not stated, and the temperature-versus-time supplementary data were unavailable to the reviewer. A fridge thermometer cannot resolve millisecond excursions of the sample.
concerns.quote: The thermometer location and time resolution should be stated in Methods. A fridge thermometer cannot resolve millisecond excursions of the sample.

concerns.concern: The current waveform at the sample is undefined. Pulse-delta mode and the stepped erase ramp are themselves trains of abrupt steps, and filtering may distort short pulses, so the abrupt-versus-smooth contrast cannot be interpreted. Pulse parameters and measured J(t) traces are needed.
concerns.quote: A nominally "smooth" ramp is therefore a train of abrupt current steps.

concerns.concern: Probe J–V sweeps go deep into flux flow. Under the authors' own picture they should re-pump or erase the state, and this is not explained.
concerns.quote: Under the authors' own picture they should re-pump or erase the state.

concerns.concern: The erase threshold has not been characterised as a function of amplitude and ramp rate.
concerns.quote: Characterise the erase threshold as a function of amplitude and ramp rate.

concerns.concern: The claim that the state persists for several hours is made without data. Retention curves at several temperatures are requested, which would also give an activation barrier.
concerns.quote: "Persists over a timescale of at least several hours" (pp. 5 and 7) is stated without any data.

concerns.concern: Endurance is shown for only about five write/erase cycles with no statistics on the spread in ΔJ and V.
concerns.quote: Fig. 1d shows only about five write/erase cycles over 400 s, with no statistics.

concerns.concern: Reading the low-Jc state involves vortex motion, and it is not shown whether readout is non-destructive in either state.
concerns.quote: Reading the low-Jc state involves finite voltage, i.e. vortex motion. Whether reading is non-destructive is not shown.

concerns.concern: The ΔJ metric uses inconsistent voltage criteria across figures, giving different magnitudes (0.2–0.8 A cm⁻²), and is partly noise-dominated near V = 0. It lacks error bars and a stated noise floor.
concerns.quote: adopt one voltage criterion above the noise floor. Give error bars from repeated cycles in Figs. 4e,f and ED Fig. 1, and state the voltage noise floor.

concerns.concern: The phenomenological model has unspecified, ad hoc parameters, including g. Its damping is chosen to peak at φ = π precisely so the phase sticks there, so it builds in the result.
concerns.quote: The damping γ(φ) is chosen to peak at φ = π precisely so that the phase "sticks" there.

concerns.concern: The physical meaning of a single Josephson phase in a junction-free mm-sized crystal is not explained. Treating γ as a proxy for the injected current J is unclear.
concerns.quote: The physical meaning of a single Josephson phase obeying φ̇ = 2eV/ħ in a mm-sized junction-free crystal is not explained.

concerns.concern: The claim that inversion symmetry requires the second minimum to sit at φ = π is incorrect. Inversion allows any symmetric pair ±φ₀.
concerns.quote: Inversion maps φ → −φ and allows any symmetric pair ±φ₀.

concerns.concern: The model is not tested against the amplitude threshold and saturation, the logarithmic duration dependence, the rate dependence or the temperature scale. Otherwise it should be presented as an illustrative cartoon.
concerns.quote: Otherwise, present the model explicitly as an illustrative cartoon.

concerns.concern: The model implies a lower flux-flow resistance in the memory state, which conflicts with the J–V branches merging at high J in Fig. 1b.
concerns.quote: Check the model's implication of a lower flux-flow resistance in the memory state against the data. In Fig. 1b the branches merge at high J.

concerns.concern: The energy-scale argument compares the 0.6 K memory cutoff with the zero-field Tc of 2.1 K. The relevant reference is the much lower Tc(B, θ) of the given sample at the measurement field.
concerns.quote: The relevant comparison is Tc(B, θ) of the given sample at 14 T, which is substantially lower, especially for RRR 44.

concerns.concern: The analogy with the intrinsic diode effect does not discriminate between mechanisms, since extrinsic metastable vortex states also anneal on warming.
concerns.quote: The analogy with the intrinsic diode effect (ref. 49) does not discriminate between mechanisms.

concerns.concern: It is untested whether the memory is a bulk effect or arises locally near contacts or edges, given non-uniform current injection from surface leads. Comparisons of contact pairs, geometries or FIB bars are requested.
concerns.quote: The memory could reside in regions near the contacts or edges, consistent with the edge-contamination picture of Paltiel et al.

concerns.concern: The strong RRR differences between the three samples are not used to discriminate an intrinsic mechanism from pinning-driven metastability. ΔJ(B) should be reported for all samples under a common protocol, including whether S3 shows the effect.
concerns.quote: An intrinsic order-parameter mechanism and a pinning-driven metastability make different predictions for how ΔJ and the field window scale with disorder.

concerns.concern: Prior history-dependent, current-pulse-switched Jc work is not cited. As a result, the claim that all-superconducting electrically controllable memory has remained elusive is inaccurate, and refs. 22–24 already demonstrate such memories and should be contrasted fairly.
concerns.quote: Refs. 22–24 already demonstrate electrically operated memories of this kind and should be contrasted fairly.

concerns.concern: The technology claims are overstated. The effect needs 7–20 T and below 0.6 K, contradicting the criticism of field-reliant schemes and the 'solely electrical' claim.
concerns.quote: This sits uneasily with the introduction's criticism of competing schemes that "rely on external magnetic field modulations"

concerns.concern: Write and erase energies are not costed, so quoting only the ~1 nW read power is misleading.
concerns.quote: The pumps (about 20 A cm⁻² for ms) and the 20 s, 40 mA erase are not costed. Quoting only the about 1 nW read power is misleading.

concerns.concern: The scaling to ≲1 pW assumes the effect survives miniaturisation, which is untested.
concerns.quote: The scaling to ≲1 pW assumes the effect survives miniaturisation, which is untested.

concerns.concern: Ref. 59, on intrinsic carrier concentration in Si, does not support the power comparison it is cited for.
concerns.quote: Ref. 59, on the intrinsic carrier concentration in Si, does not support the power comparison.

concerns.concern: The wording about metastability is internally inconsistent across the abstract, main text and Methods.
concerns.quote: The abstract says "metastable state". p. 7 says "does not appear to be transiently metastable".

concerns.concern: The text says the S2 memory window extends to just below 20 T, but the figures show it vanishing by about 17 T.
concerns.quote: p. 9 says the S2 window extends to "just below 20 T", but Fig. 4e and ED Fig. 8 show ΔJ vanishing by about 17 T.

concerns.concern: The temperature range quoted for Fig. 3 in the text does not match the figure. Fig. 3b spans 0.05–0.6 K, and the 1.0 K data come from S1 with a different protocol.
concerns.quote: p. 8 says Fig. 3 covers 50 mK–1.0 K for amplitude tuning. Fig. 3b spans 0.05–0.6 K.

concerns.concern: There are figure unit and label errors, such as wrong axis units and inconsistent symbols. Inconsistent α ranges, colour bars and the definition of J/α also need clarification.
concerns.quote: ED Fig. 1a x-axis "J_ex (ms)" should be A cm⁻².

concerns.concern: Methods contains a typo: the global minimum is written at π = 0 instead of φ = 0.
concerns.quote: "The global minimum at π = 0" should read φ = 0.

concerns.concern: Several physics statements are misworded. 'Minimise entropy' should be free energy, intervortex interactions are conflated with pinning, and the Bean model is not determined by total energy imparted.
concerns.quote: "Minimise entropy" (p. 13) should be "free energy".

concerns.concern: Sample dimensions, cross-sections, contact separations and the current-density conversion factor are missing for each sample.
concerns.quote: Sample dimensions, cross-sections, contact separations and the J-conversion factor should be given for each sample.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1b protocol insets are hard to read. Explicit J(t) traces should show whether each down-sweep after a probe was abrupt.
concerns.quote: The protocol insets are hard to read. Explicit J(t) traces for each panel would help

concerns.concern: Two references (26 and 57, Blatter et al.) are duplicates.
concerns.quote: Refs. 26 and 57 are identical (Blatter et al.).

concerns.concern: Fig. 4h, on sample S3, is not connected to any memory measurement. Its relevance should be stated or the panel moved.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4h (S3, ac, 400 mK) is not connected to any memory measurement on S3.

concerns.concern: The simulation code and data-processing scripts for the ΔJ heatmaps are not provided alongside the measurement code.
concerns.quote: The simulation code and raw-data processing scripts used for the ΔJ heatmaps should be provided alongside the measurement code.
